description: Provenance for the draft FHGM conformance suite. The suite is model-level: it validates FHGM records embedded in files carrying a released FHGFF3 identity against the reviewed native draft contract. The sealed expectations were observed against the FHGFF3 1.1 bytes and stay bound to them; the matrix lane (base_matrix.json) re-observes identity-rewritten twins against the FHGFF3 1.2 bytes per the maintainer dual-base decision of 2026-11-15. The suite depends on two released external artifacts (the two base-schema releases registered in development/model/base-schemas.json) and on the contract and generator bytes carried in this repository. scripts/check_header_parity.py applies the same discipline to the pinned header/ tree; run_conformance.py verifies every digest below on each run and refuses to report a pass when a recorded artifact changed under the manifest. Nothing here is a schema authority: FHGM has no released contract, no schemaVersion, no schema URL and no versions.json row, and selection rule V7 keeps it that way until the shared publication PR lands.

baseRegistry.role: the checker's authority for which FHGFF3 base bytes may be supplied and how a carrier's declared schemaVersion selects among them
baseRegistry.note: provenance.json mirrors the two base records below for the suite lanes; run_conformance.py cross-checks registry, provenance record, checker-supplied bytes and each file's actual digest on every run and refuses on any disagreement. Released material is recorded by tag with the tag->commit resolution; no floating branch is recorded for any release.

baseSchema.commitNote: The commit the v0.5.0 tag names. It is not an ancestor of shared main: the v0.5.0 release was tagged before its merge commit landed, a split recorded in the workspace guide and not repeated for later releases.
baseSchema.crossCheck: base-schemas.json registers the same digest and validate_fhgm.py resolves every supplied --base-schema file against that registry, refusing any other bytes; run_conformance.py compares this record, that registry, the supplied files and their actual digests and reports all of them. The released file is also what development/examples/contract, development/examples/model and development/examples/s6k were validated against in PRs #7, #10 and #11.
baseSchema.whyThisRelease: These bytes remain the sealed lane's base: every expectation in manifest.json was observed against them and keeps its evidence trail for the v0.8.0 review. The 2026-11-15 dual-base decision adds the v0.6.0 bytes as the matrix lane's base; it does not repoint this record, and the sealed vectors keep their 1.1 identity bytes unchanged.

matrixBaseSchema.commitNote: The commit the v0.6.0 annotated tag names (tag object ab7e3ddd..., dereferenced 2026-11-15 via the Git refs API). Unlike v0.5.0 it is an ancestor of shared main.
matrixBaseSchema.pathNote: Root path. schemas/fhgff3.json returns 404 at this ref, measured 2026-11-15; a nonsense-version control (v9.9.9 on both paths) also 404s, so the 200s above are tag-resolution, not server defaults.
matrixBaseSchema.verification: Fetched by tag name and by resolved commit URL over HTTPS as full downloads; cmp-verified byte-equal to each other; sha256 equals the workspace guide's v0.6.0 release-tarball record (1942be4c...). A full JSON walk of both releases found the real delta: the schemaVersion enum gains '1.2'; Completeness.lineageDataset gains dotted BUSCO dataset versions (pattern ^[a-z0-9_]+_odb[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$) for carriers declaring 1.2; two new version-gated if/then clauses keep stating the old pattern for carriers declaring 1.0 or 1.1; description text updated. No FHGM vector or fixture byte carries a completeness object, so the delta touches no FHGM content, and the 1.0 extension floor (docs/FORMAT.md R15 clause) is byte-identical in both releases.
matrixBaseSchema.crossCheck: base-schemas.json registers the same digest; validate_fhgm.py selects these bytes only for carriers declaring schemaVersion '1.2' (or judging a superseded declaration as the only supplied candidate); run_conformance.py compares this record, the registry and the supplied file's actual digest on every --matrix run.
matrixBaseSchema.whyThisRelease: Maintainer decision 2026-11-15: FHGM must be describable on both released FHGFF3 bases, because the released toolkit (fair-bioheaders 0.11.0) writes 1.2 headers today while the merged fixtures and the sealed manifest carry 1.1 bytes. The 1.2 lane is an added matrix, not a repoint: no sealed expectation moves.

contractArtifacts.note: Reviewed in place on 2026-11-14: the 2026-11-12 proposal bytes (commit 8b0ca00, sha256 9114780bfcc8b575fa660b2d38a7ad521d9b993d2544963cdad388daed045e27) carry the same title, field names, requiredness and keywords; only description text changed to record the review's positions, so no validation outcome moved and the draft label stays v0.1. The dual-base work of 2026-11-15 leaves these bytes unchanged: the record contract carries no file identity, which is exactly the transport framing (FHGM is not a header type; records ride inside an FHGFF3 header and model records carry no schema field).

contractArtifacts.role: model-level checker (K3-K6) and base selector, the authority for every recorded outcome
base-release registry consulted for every supplied --base-schema file

vectorGenerators.role: generates the v0.1 fixture set that this suite cites in place (PR #11 bytes, unchanged)
derives the S6k record vector from the committed profile fixture
shared render, canonical-JSON and checksum helpers reused by both generators (PR #4 pilot machinery)

observedWith.note: Every sealed-lane outcome comes from a run of development/model/validate_fhgm.py with these versions. check_draft.py was additionally re-run with fair-bioheaders 0.8.1 (the shared conformance job's toolkit baseline in this repository's header-parity.yml), and run_conformance.py passed end to end under 0.8.1 as well, so no sealed outcome depends on a toolkit newer than the one that job installs. The 2026-11-15 dual-base rework re-observed both lanes under the same versions (0.11.0 toolkit; the checker imports the toolkit's header reader and checksum implementation; the matrix lane's twins are derived with the standard library only). The GFF3 feature lane was observed twice: with gff3-validator 0.1.0 built from the local gff3-validator checkout and with the 0.1.0 wheel installed from PyPI (the CI environment); both report zero errors and zero warnings on all 31 vectors, and the matrix lane repeats that observation on the 31 twins.

independence.checksum: run_conformance.py recomputes each vector's file-bound SHA-512/256 with hashlib over the exact bytes minus the root checksum line, as a second implementation next to the toolkit's, and requires the two to agree with the value the header states before it reports the model layer. For the matrix lane the twins are derived from the sealed bytes by a standard-library line rewrite plus the same independent recomputation, so the twin digests this file's matrix seals are verifiable without the toolkit.
independence.vectorOutcomes: No expectation in manifest.json was written from reading the code. Each one was observed by running the committed checker over the generated bytes, and run_conformance.py re-observes it on every run. base_matrix.json follows the same discipline for the 1.2 lane: every entry is a recorded observation of the committed checker over the derived twin bytes, sealed with --seal-matrix only after a clean run.
independence.notRun: gff3-validate 0.1.0 (local checkout build and the PyPI wheel) ran the feature layer over every vector; the lane is optional at run time and reports skipped where the tool is absent. Header checks were deliberately skipped with --no-header, because the FHGFF3 header identity is the base layer of this suite, not its subject.

syntheticContent.statement: Every vector except s6k-derived-record-fixture is synthetic. The accession SYNTHETIC_ASSEMBLY.1 and the SeqCol digest come from the revision pilot's one-record toy collection (>toy with 100 'A' bases), the accessions, model IDs, DOIs, URNs and evidence strings are placeholders scoped to these directories, and the synthetic FHR parent digest is computed over declared synthetic bytes. No accession, digest, identifier or biological relationship was invented for a real resource. The matrix twins inherit exactly their source vector's content with the two released-identity lines rewritten and the checksum recomputed; they invent nothing.
syntheticContent.attribution: s6k-derived-record-fixture wraps a feature payload derived from Laura K. Reed, 'Model: Gene model for the ortholog of S6k in Drosophila ananassae', CaltechDATA v1.0, CC BY 4.0 (deposit https://doi.org/10.22002/e86gh-a7p16), as recorded in development/examples/s6k/README.md. Its record reuses only identifiers, attribution and the verified reference result already recorded there.

downstreamPins.name: JavaScript library draft-lane transport-overlay pin
downstreamPins.asOf: 2026-11-15, re-verified against the consumer's server main the same day: the pin records sha256 dd9f69274f26860bbfd71d0e8b2794420c5369fb5d40ce838fb6a9e6d5116e3d (the single-identity overlay, suiteCommit ac3d37b). The dual-base overlay changes these bytes, so the pin and the consumer's vendored copy fhgm-transport-draft.json go stale when this change merges; the consumer's src/fhgm.js already treats R15 as admitting 1.2 carriers, per its own note. The record-contract pin on the same main (sha256 bf1553ca...) tracks bytes this change leaves untouched and stays fresh. Scope of the same merge's staleness, reported not fixed here: JavaScript main does NOT yet field-pin our manifest - a suiteManifestSha256 pin for the 31-vector manifest exists only on that repository's unmerged draft-lane branch and will move when that branch rebases onto the new bytes - and Tools-R main vendors byte copies of the suite (tests/draft/fhgm/: manifest 31f14f02..., provenance.json, the vector files) checked by its own tools/check_vendoring.R; the vendored manifest and provenance move at merge while every vendored vector file stays byte-identical, because no manifest vector entry changes. Every refresh is the consumer's action against the merged commit, never an FHGM-side edit.
downstreamPins.checkedBy: run_conformance.py --check-downstream-pins (network; scheduled and dispatch only, so PR lanes stay offline)
